To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glutamate uptake occurs at the early stage of synaptic transmission, and that the glutamate uptake occurs by the v-ATPase-dependent mechanism.
the glutamate uptake activity is similar for CCVs and SVs, that the uptake requires ATP, Cl- and the v-ATPase, and that the uptake is sensitive to glutamate transporters blockers.
glutamate transporters on clathrin coated vesicles (CCV) may play a role in the recycling of synaptic vesicles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of neurotransmitter release and recycling in nerve terminals, with a particular emphasis on synaptic vesicle recycling and the role of synaptic endosomes.
understanding how synaptic vesicles recycle in the nerve terminal.
the molecular mechanisms of neurotransmitter uptake into synaptic vesicles and the recycling of synaptic vesicles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
synaptic vesicles and CCVs are functionally equivalent in their capacity to take up the neurotransmitter glutamate.

synaptic vesicle recycling in nerve terminals involves two steps: first, synaptic vesicle membrane is retrieved by clathrin-mediated endocytosis, then, the retrieved vesicles are reloaded with neurotransmitter in the cytoplasm by a v-ATPase-driven proton pump.
synaptic vesicles recycle via a clathrin-coat vesicular pathway, which is consistent with the hypothesis that synaptic vesicles are formed at a late stage of endosomal maturation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CCV is the first intermediate of synaptic vesicle endocytosis that is capable of glutamate uptake.
glutamate uptake occurs at a very early stage in synaptic vesicle recycling.
the recycling pathway for synaptic vesicles is more direct than previously appreciated, with a minimum number of intermediate steps.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ability to recycle neurotransmitter is an inherent property of the synaptic vesicle itself, and is not a function of the endosomal system.
the recycling vesicles can be filled up with neurotransmitter before they become releasable vesicles.
the recycling pathway is a very efficient process.
